title: ISO 9001: 2015 Transition Training: Quality Management System
overview: The ISO 9001:2015 Quality Management System standard is globally recognized and adaptable to both manufacturing and service industries. It provides organizations, regardless of size, with a robust framework to demonstrate compliance with international standards.

In today's competitive landscape, governments, industry bodies, and large corporations increasingly require their supply chain partners to adopt the principles of ISO 9001:2015. Whether you are part of the supply chain or require your partners to align with this standard, understanding its requirements is essential. This course emphasizes the Risk-Based and Process Approaches, guiding participants on how to align these principles with their business for maximum benefit.
This program offers comprehensive guidance on transitioning from ISO 9001:2008 to ISO 9001:2015, enabling participants to meet the new standard's requirements before the implementation deadline.
audience: This course is ideal for anyone managing, interacting with, or auditing ISO 9001 Quality Management Systems. This includes, but is not limited to:
Quality, QHSE, Compliance, and Assurance staff
Professionals new to Quality Management seeking a comprehensive understanding of the new standard and the transition process
methodology: The course uses a blend of interactive PowerPoint presentations, real-life case studies, practical examples, and open discussions to cover both theoretical and practical aspects of the transition process.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Develop a Business Risk and Opportunities Register tailored to their organization.
Conduct a Gap Analysis assessment of their existing Quality Management System.
Advise leadership on the key principles outlined in Clause 5 of ISO 9001:2015.
Implement best practices to transition and integrate the system effectively across their organization.
Recognize the impact of human factors on system implementation and effectiveness.
